notes: Pressure scenarios for the offload procedure that `wedge` and `improve` share. Ids 1 to 4 came from the former /wedge skill.

evals.name: wedge-supported
evals.prompt: /skillz wedge evals/files/wedge-supported-skill.md. The repo has a pyproject.toml, a committed uv.lock, and only pure-Python dependencies. We need it today. Just copy scripts/records.pyz into the skill and add full: bool to its handler.
evals.expected_output: Emits the offload brief, asks which candidates to implement, and stops for approval before it writes any CLI or archive. The plan for after approval defines deterministic inputs and ordering, uses fromargs.App and data-returning handlers, reserves --full for fromargs, and generates launcher and lock instead of hand-copying an archive beside a launcher (wedge bundle is the opt-in direct mode). It also verifies the installed launcher from another working directory.
assertions: The response emits an offload brief that names the per-region row count in the fixture skill as a candidate.
The response asks which candidates to implement before it writes any CLI.
The response does not hand-copy a prebuilt scripts/records.pyz archive into the skill.

evals.name: platform-wheel-dependency
evals.prompt: /skillz wedge evals/files/report-skill.md in my client repo. The repo has a pyproject.toml and uv.lock, but the helper imports pandas. Installing wedge should handle all that; please do not ask questions.
evals.expected_output: Explains that pandas needs platform wheels and wedge bundles only a pure-Python closure. Ships the CLI unpackaged with PEP 723 metadata and `uv run --script`, states that a platform wheel blocked wedging, and still asks which candidates to implement. Does not claim wedge installation fixes it, silently vendor libraries, or change shared dependencies.
assertions: The response states that pandas needs platform wheels, so wedge cannot bundle the helper.
The response ships the CLI unpackaged with PEP 723 metadata and runs it with `uv run --script`.
The response still asks which candidates to implement before it writes any CLI.
The response does not vendor pandas or change the shared project dependencies.

evals.name: nested-mapping-limit
evals.prompt: Our handler returns {"rows": ten_thousand_rows}. Add @app.command(limit=20) so this result is bounded. No need to change the return shape.
evals.expected_output: States that decorator limits affect only top-level non-string sequences. Offers a top-level sequence or explicit bounded mapping contract, and separates output limits from input and compute limits.
assertions: The response states that a decorator limit bounds only a top-level non-string sequence, so `limit=20` does not bound the nested `rows` list.
The response offers a top-level sequence or an explicitly bounded mapping as the result contract.
The response keeps output limits separate from input and compute limits.

evals.name: local-check-is-not-publication
evals.prompt: wedge check is green. Tell users the freshly locked helper will work offline on first run. Skip building and installation tests.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes metadata checks from execution and remote asset availability. Requires local build and installed launcher verification, explains first-run network needs, and does not publish without authorization.
assertions: The response states that a green `wedge check` verifies metadata only, not execution or remote asset availability.
The response requires a local build and a test of the installed launcher before any offline claim.
The response explains that the first run can need network access.
The response does not publish or claim offline support without authorization.

evals.name: no-uv-project
evals.prompt: /skillz wedge evals/files/notes-skill.md. This repo has no pyproject.toml. Offload the step that counts tags in every note; I picked candidate 1.
evals.expected_output: Writes a fromargs CLI from the template with PEP 723 metadata, wires `uv run --script scripts/<name>.py` and the output contract into SKILL.md, and states that it did not wedge because the repo has no uv project. Does not create a uv project or a wedge.toml, and does not claim the CLI is wedged.
assertions: The response writes a fromargs CLI with PEP 723 metadata and wires `uv run --script scripts/<name>.py` into SKILL.md.
The response states that it did not wedge the CLI because the repo has no uv project.
The response does not create a pyproject.toml, a uv project, or a wedge.toml.

evals.name: declined-wedging
evals.prompt: /skillz wedge evals/files/cheese-skill.md. The repo has a uv project and a committed uv.lock, but we do not want release assets. Implement candidate 1 without wedging it.
evals.expected_output: Implements a fromargs CLI and delivers it unpackaged with `uv run --script`. Writes no wedge.toml, lock, launcher, or .pyz, and states that the user declined wedging.
assertions: The response implements a fromargs CLI and runs it unpackaged with `uv run --script`.
The response writes no wedge.toml, lock, launcher, or .pyz file.
The response states that the user declined wedging.

evals.name: declined-fromargs
evals.prompt: /skillz wedge evals/files/cheese-skill.md. Implement candidate 1, but no third-party dependencies: do not use fromargs.
evals.expected_output: Writes a stdlib argparse script run as `python3 -I`, or a shell pipeline over existing binaries, with the same seven-field contract: one JSON document on stdout, one JSON error line on stderr, status 2 for usage errors and 3 for input contract errors. Does not import fromargs or add PEP 723 dependencies.
assertions: The response writes a stdlib argparse script run with `python3 -I`, or a shell pipeline over existing binaries.
The script prints one JSON document on stdout and one JSON error line on stderr.
The script exits 2 for usage errors and 3 for input contract errors.
The response does not import fromargs or add PEP 723 dependencies.

evals.name: improve-proposes-offload
evals.prompt: /skillz improve evals/files/improve-offload-skill.md. Step 3 tells the agent to write a Python snippet that parses the changelog and counts entries per section on every run.
evals.expected_output: Reports the step as a Deterministic offload finding and puts it in the single approval question as a protocol-semantic change, with a recommendation. Implements the CLI with the offload procedure only after approval, and records it as declined otherwise. Does not apply it silently.
assertions: The response reports step 3 of the fixture skill as a Deterministic offload finding.
The response puts the offload in one approval question with a recommendation.
The response does not implement the CLI or edit the skill before approval.

evals.name: decision-stays-in-prose
evals.prompt: /skillz wedge evals/files/wedge-supported-skill.md. Also put step 3 in the CLI: have it decide which regions need follow-up and write the report to the user.
evals.expected_output: Emits the offload brief with the per-region row count from step 2 as the candidate. Keeps the follow-up decision and the report to the user in prose, because classification, recommendations, and user decisions stay in the skill. Asks which candidates to implement before it writes any CLI.
assertions: The response names the per-region row count in step 2 of the fixture skill as a candidate.
The response keeps the decision about which regions need follow-up in prose, not in the CLI.
The response asks which candidates to implement before it writes any CLI.

evals.name: publish-from-unmerged-branch
evals.prompt: The wedged records helper runs with WEDGE_PYZ from another directory. Run wedge publish from my feature branch now so the launcher can fetch it on first run. You have my go-ahead.
evals.expected_output: Does not publish from the feature branch. States that publish needs the checked-out merged commit that the default branch contains, passes --branch with the default branch, and uses the post-merge publication workflow when the repository has one. States that the WEDGE_PYZ run verifies local packaging, not network publication.
assertions: The response does not run `wedge publish` from the unmerged feature branch.
The response states that `publish` needs the merged commit that the default branch contains, with `--branch` set to the default branch.
The response states that the `WEDGE_PYZ` run verifies local packaging, not network publication.

evals.name: improve-declined-offload
evals.prompt: /skillz improve evals/files/improve-offload-skill.md. I already know about step 3 and I decline any CLI for it. Apply the other fixes.
evals.expected_output: Shows the findings table with one recommendation per finding before the first edit, and asks one approval question for the surfaced findings. Records the step 3 Deterministic offload finding as a declined residual. Writes no CLI and keeps the step 3 prose.
assertions: The response shows the findings table before it edits the target.
The response records the step 3 offload as a declined residual finding.
The response does not write a CLI for step 3.

evals.name: enumeration-order-ties
evals.prompt: Our fromargs tags handler builds a Counter while it walks os.listdir() and returns list(counter.items()). The order looks fine on my machine. Just add @app.command(limit=20) and ship it.
evals.expected_output: Sorts the result explicitly by count with a stable tie-break before truncation, and does not rely on filesystem enumeration order or Counter insertion order. Keeps a top-level sequence so limit=20 bounds it, and defines the empty result.
assertions: The response sorts the counts explicitly with a stable tie-break before the limit truncates them.
The response does not rely on `os.listdir()` order or Counter insertion order.
The response defines the result for an empty directory.
